Tasks.description: A Task is the application of an action to a process activity (workflow). It serves only as an execution template; concrete Jobs are created from Tasks in the Workspace module (where taskOwner, taskStatus, taskDueDate and projectID are set).

attributes.name: taskID
attributes.notes: Auto-generated primary key

attributes.name: eventID
attributes.notes: Event that triggered this task

attributes.name: processID
attributes.notes: Stored FK (materialize-FK convention) — the process of the selected event; the form filters the options by the Event field. The old "rollup: from eventID" prose made the parser resolve the TARGET as the Events table (fuzzy id-suffix match), so the Process select offered eventIDs (2026-08-04 bug).

attributes.name: workflowID
attributes.notes: Options filtered by matching processID

attributes.name: actionID
attributes.rule: computed: lookup Actions via activityID (display: actionName)

attributes.name: predecessorTask
attributes.notes: Self-referential task ordering (issue #302; nullable — the first task of a process has no predecessor). Unlike Workflows there is NO constrain/indentationRule dimension: every task link is start-to-finish (sequential). The form select offers the tasks of the selected Process.

attributes.name: taskIndentationID
attributes.notes: Derived task outline number (1.0.1, 1.1.2, 2.0.1…) — never stored (issue #302): the workflow step's indentationID is the base, padded to two segments when it is a single major number (1 → 1.0 — the planned Gantt webhook consumers need a fixed depth), and the task's sequence within the SAME step (predecessorTask chain) appends as the last segment. A predecessor in ANOTHER step does not sub-number — the counter restarts per step (the issue's T04 example). Every Tasks subitem context orders by this value.

attributes.name: requirementName
attributes.notes: Derived — requirements of the task's procedures (doctrine: tasks are requirement-free, the procedure carries the requirement set; empty set = applies to all, Q1)

attributes.name: functionID
attributes.notes: multivalued — derived from the competences referencing this task

attributes.name: executionTime
attributes.notes: Derived — procedures create the variance in task duration (Rafael, 04/08): the requirement set changes how long a task takes, so the time is registered PER PROCEDURE and the task shows the sum of its procedures.

attributes.name: competenceID
attributes.rule: rollup -> Competence via: taskID -> functionID (display: competenceName)
attributes.notes: multivalued

attributes.name: userID
attributes.notes: multivalued — derived live (issue #214): People holding a CERTIFIED Onboarding (isCertified==true) on a task-compatible competence, whose combined competences cover ALL the requirements the task derives from its procedures (union of the requirement sets; a wildcard procedure covers everything) — the certified-responsible doctrine at the Tasks level. Authored 2026-08-19 as prose ('users that have the competences that matches all the requirements for the procedure applied to the task', constraint isCertified==true); normalized to the CERTIFIED-USERS rule kind (certifiedUsersForTask in resolve.js). Ticket context (issue #233): rendered inside a Ticket's Tasks tab, coverage must ALSO span the ticket's live inherited requirement set (#226) — the subitem accessor passes ticketRequirements(ticket) as extra ids; the standalone Tasks dashboard stays task-level. Procedure-status gate (sv71): a competence whose whole procedure group is non-Approved is INERT — it contributes no coverage until the method is Approved, and a non-Approved wildcard no longer certifies everything.

attributes.name: procedureRegistry
attributes.notes: The single procedure the requirement context selects for the task (issue #270): inside a Ticket's Tasks tab the context is the ticket's live inherited requirement set (#226) — candidates are the task's procedures whose requirementID[] covers ALL the ticket requirements (AND semantics, not OR; an empty set is the Q1 wildcard and covers everything). Exactly one candidate renders its procedureRegistry as a pill tag; zero or several render GAP (no unambiguous documented method for the combination — including a wildcard procedure coexisting with a specific one). The subitem accessor passes ticketRequirements(ticket) (mapSubitem in app.js, the #233 pattern); the standalone Tasks drawer falls back to the task-level set (unique procedure or GAP). ticketProcedureForTask in resolve.js.

attributes.name: roles
attributes.notes: multivalued

attributes.name: procedureID
attributes.notes: Procedures registered for this task (subitem tab). Visible column since issue #271: a task with NO procedure is a gap — the empty rollup renders the GAP caution tag (gap-tag flag). Header overridden to the plural 'Procedures' (humanize would collide with the #270 'Procedure' column, the single ticket-context resolution). Kept out of the ticket Tasks tab (subitem-display false) — there the #270 column already carries the contextual GAP signal.

attributes.name: taskOwner
attributes.notes: Accountability owner (ISO 9001:2015 §5.3, §6.2.2(c))

Procedures.description: Documented method for executing a Task (ISO 9001:2015 §4.4 operations chain; §7.5 documented information). Tasks stay requirement-free — the procedure is where requirements bite: each row registers how a task is performed under a given requirement set, with its own input/output handouts. An empty requirement list means the procedure applies to every requirement (Q1 wildcard).

attributes.name: roles

People.description: Individual users and team members (ISO §5.3 / §7.1.2). All *Owner foreign keys across the model resolve to a Person.

attributes.name: businessUnitID

attributes.name: departmentID

attributes.name: countryName

attributes.name: hireDate

attributes.name: workingHours

Onboarding.description: Tracks a person's certification progress against the competences derived from their function and roles (ISO §7.2).

attributes.name: onboardID
attributes.notes: Auto-generated primary key

attributes.name: onboardingTitle
attributes.notes: Context label for the certified competence GROUP (issue #239) — first *Title attr, so it is the table label (and therefore required in the form)

attributes.name: departmentID
attributes.notes: Department running the onboarding; businessUnitID derives from it on save

attributes.name: roleID
attributes.notes: Role resolved from the onboarding's function (Roles.functionID); display: roleName via the Roles table which owns that field.

attributes.name: levelRank
attributes.notes: Ordering key (1 = lowest)

attributes.name: competenceID
attributes.notes: multivalued — the competence GROUP this onboarding certifies (1:many since issue #239; isCertified covers the whole group). Stores competence PKs; displayed by the user-given competenceTitle since issue #284. Role/rank/department narrowing lives in the form cascade (the old 'via: roleID + levelRank' spelling made the select store roleIDs)

attributes.name: isCertified
attributes.notes: Certification gate — a person only qualifies for the Tasks Users column (CERTIFIED-USERS, issue #214) and the Jobs Responsible control when this is true. BOOLEAN-select convention (issue #218): the form renders fixed Yes/No options and stores a real boolean.

attributes.name: requirementName
attributes.rule: computed: Competence via competenceID (display: FOREACH([{requirementTypeName: requirementName}]))

attributes.name: onboardingOwner
attributes.notes: Accountability owner (ISO 9001:2015 §5.3, §6.2.2(c))

Title.tooltip: Names the competence group this onboarding certifies

Talent.field-rule: SelectLabel = functionName; filtered by departmentID selected

Competence.tooltip: Competences of the selected Department (via their event) matching the chosen Role
Competence.field-rule: SelectLabel = processName; filtered by departmentID + roleID selected

Certified.tooltip: Certifies the whole competence group of this onboarding

Competence.description: Competence profile mapping skills to roles, scopes and products (ISO §7.2), derived largely from the Tasks a role performs.

attributes.name: competenceTitle
attributes.notes: User-given label for the competence (issue #284) — with the procedure GROUP cardinality the title is what distinguishes and groups competences; first *Title attr, so it is the table label (and therefore required in the form)

attributes.name: departmentID
attributes.notes: Derived on save from the selected Event (Event.departmentID) — join key for the Onboarding Department → Competence cascade

attributes.name: processID
attributes.notes: Process context for the certified task

attributes.name: productScopeID
attributes.notes: The product scope this competence certifies (scope × product group in one key — replaces the separate Scope/Product Group selects, issue #159 follow-up). Options = the selected process's list.

attributes.name: scopeID
attributes.notes: Derived — the scope of the certified product scope

attributes.name: skillLevelID
attributes.notes: Required proficiency

attributes.name: roleID
attributes.notes: Filtered by the selected function + skill level in the form

attributes.name: levelRank
attributes.notes: Step of the professional INSIDE the competence's skill level (Rafael, 03/08): rank 1 = a newly promoted/hired professional at that level may hold the competence; holding rank 3 on every competence of a skill level signals readiness to move up a level (promotion automation: issue #149)

attributes.name: taskID
attributes.notes: Task this competence certifies; options filtered by event + process

attributes.name: actionID
attributes.notes: Via taskID

attributes.name: activityID
attributes.notes: Via taskID

attributes.name: productGroupID
attributes.notes: Derived — the product group of the certified product scope (renders the productName | SPECS display)

attributes.name: productSpecID
attributes.notes: multivalued — spec definitions certified by this competence

attributes.name: productSpecName
attributes.rule: computed: Product Specs via productSpecID (display: specName)

attributes.name: procedureID
attributes.notes: multivalued — the procedure GROUP this competence certifies (1:many since issue #284, reverting the #231 1:1; group restricted to the competence's TASK — the picker filters by Task). The quality manager's requirement decision lives on the Procedure; the competence inherits the UNION of its procedures' sets, and a procedure with an EMPTY set (Q1 wildcard) in the group makes the competence certify every requirement (decision kept in #284).

attributes.name: requirementID
attributes.notes: Derived — requirements certified through the linked procedure GROUP: the UNION of the procedures' sets (1:many since issue #284; a procedure with an empty set applies to all, Q1 — one wildcard procedure in the group certifies everything). Doctrine (issue #231, kept in #284): a requirement NEVER enters a competence automatically — the quality manager decides on the Procedure (its Requirements picker already offers the context-aligned options), and the competence inherits the procedures' sets. Legacy stored requirementID still honoured as fallback when no procedure is linked.

attributes.name: competenceName
attributes.rule: computed: CONCAT([taskName],' for ',[scopeName],' of ',[productGroupName],' applied to ',[{requirementTypeName: requirementName}])
attributes.notes: Rendered from the CONCAT rule at display time (not stored)

attributes.name: channelName
attributes.rule: computed: list of channelName of every input and output handout of the linked procedures

attributes.name: resources
attributes.notes: Training resource/modality, e.g. e-learning (nullable)

attributes.name: competenceOwner
attributes.notes: Accountability owner (ISO 9001:2015 §5.3, §6.2.2(c))

Title.tooltip: Names the competence — distinguishes and groups competences now that one competence certifies a group of procedures

Role.field-rule: filtered by Skill Level + Function selected

Product Scope.tooltip: Product scope this competence certifies — offered from the selected process's list (scope and product group derive from it)

Procedure.tooltip: The procedures of the selected task that this competence certifies (group, 1:many — the union of their requirement sets is inherited)

Job Family.description: Job family a role or resource belongs to — the HR-management standard grouping (ISO §7.2). Renamed from Graduation (issue #166): education titles/institutions added no value to the model.

attributes.name: jobFamilyName
attributes.notes: e.g., Electrical Design, Mechanical Design (issue #166 — was graduationTitle)

attributes.name: field
attributes.notes: e.g., Engineering, Technical

attributes.name: jobFamilyOwner
attributes.notes: Accountability owner (ISO 9001:2015 §5.3, §6.2.2(c))
